nodes.label: Build Progress Log
nodes.rationale: Per-stage record of files created, acceptance criteria met, open questions and deviations. Maintained at the end of every stage before committing, as the build plan requires.

nodes.label: Stage Ledger 0 to 28
nodes.rationale: Stages 0-14 built the logic under the build plan; 15-24 are defined in the roadmap; 25-28 were added later. Complete: 0-14, 16-19, 25-28. Remaining: 20 (hardening), 21 (deployment), 22 (Arabic/RTL), 24 (pre-launch); 15 and 23 are partial.

nodes.label: Open Questions Q1 to Q11
nodes.rationale: Per build-plan rule 4, a stage that depends on an unanswered question implements the documented assumption, adds a TODO(open-question) comment, and records it here rather than silently deciding. Q2 (bill amounts), Q3 (expiry), Q4 (priority reservations), Q7 (manager write access), Q8 (claim code lifetime) and Q11 (native vs installable) remain open.

nodes.label: Q1 — What the QR Code Does
nodes.rationale: Answered three times. Confirmed 2026-07-30 that the code identifies the member; reversed 2026-08-08 to no QR at all with a benefit-request flow; re-answered 2026-08-12 with a static code on the back of the printed card, recovered from commit 2f44daf~1 rather than rewritten. The alternative reading — a code displayed at each outlet and scanned by the member — would have made a 40% discount self-declared.

nodes.label: Q5 — Staff MFA Gap
nodes.rationale: The one place where the build plan's closed six-endpoint auth list and the security document's 'without exception' requirement pointed in different directions: inventing an MFA flow would violate rule 2 to satisfy rule 3. Flagged rather than silently resolved, then closed in Stage 19 with TOTP, encrypted secrets, recovery codes and a separate challenge JWT audience.

nodes.label: Q6 — Passcode Delivery Channel
nodes.rationale: Originally no provider was named anywhere, and the plaintext code was deliberately never logged or returned rather than weakening the control for testing convenience. Closed in Stage 18 by email over SMTP, with the caveat that an administrator must record a member's email at creation time while this is the channel.

nodes.label: Staff Management Was Never Built
nodes.rationale: The build plan lists staff management in Stage 12; it did not exist. Three consequences: instant revocation from the dashboard could not be performed, breached-password screening could not be implemented because nothing set a password, and there was no MFA reset. Recorded rather than quietly widening scope, and suggested as Stage 25.

nodes.label: Environment Deviations
nodes.rationale: Docker is not installed on the development machine, so docker-compose.yml is written but unverified and a temporary PostgreSQL 18.4 cluster on 127.0.0.1:5434 stands in with pgp_owner and pgp_app roles mirroring the compose setup. Compose publishes on 5433 because 5432 is taken.

nodes.label: Deviations from Spec
nodes.rationale: Exactly two: Member.tokenVersion added beyond the build plan's Stage 1 schema, and HS256 rather than EdDSA/RS256 for access token signing. Both traced to explicit clauses in the security document. Q5 and Q6 are gaps, not silent deviations — both were flagged rather than built around.

nodes.label: Seeded Benefit Values
nodes.rationale: fnb 25%, rooms 30%, spa 40%, events 25%, lifestyle 30%, with guest caps and reservation numbers taken from the product definition and the printed benefits sheet. No percentage, cap or phone number appears in application code — that is R14.

nodes.label: Outlet Fulfilment Delivery Summary
nodes.rationale: Two client requests built together because the second is only useful once the first exists: a request stops being a petition, and outlets get their own screen at apps/web-outlet. Also cleared two pre-existing blockers — a publisher.ts narrowing gap that broke the production image build, and the test suite inheriting OTP_DELIVERY_CHANNEL from a developer's .env.
